pages.text: Long ago, sending a message meant writing a letter by hand.
Letters traveled by foot, horse, or ship across long distances.
Sometimes letters took weeks or months to arrive.
In the 1800s, the telegraph sent messages using electric signals.
Messages traveled as dots and dashes across long wires.
Soon, the telephone let people hear voices from far away.
Radio and television shared news and stories with many families at once.
Later, computers connected through the internet.
Today, messages can travel around the world in seconds.
From letters to internet, communication became faster and easier.
